question.text: Which of the following is NOT an advantage of e-voting over traditional postal ballot voting?

answer.text: Immediate declaration of results after voting closes
Requirement for shareholders to visit the registered office to cast their votes
Increased shareholder participation in corporate decisions

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists the advantages of e-voting as immediate declaration of results, elimination of paper and postal delays, the ability to vote at a convenient time and place or from home/office, increased shareholder participation, and reduction in administrative costs. The Trap: "Requirement for shareholders to visit the registered office" is the opposite of an e-voting advantage — the whole point of e-voting is to avoid the need for physical presence at the registered office to cast a vote. Note: The listed e-voting advantages (immediate results, elimination of paper/postal delays, voting at a convenient time/place or from home/office, increased participation and reduction in administrative costs) are covered on pages 160-161 of the NISM-Series-II-A Registrars and Transfer Agents (Corporate) Certification Examination workbook (October 2025).
